author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A 43-year-old Osterville man pleaded not guilty Monday after prosecutors accused him of driving drunk and striking a Barnstable police officer outside a concert in Hyannis, WHDH reported.

Robert Brando-Hunt faces charges of operating under the influence of liquor as a second offense, operating under the influence with serious injury and negligence, and negligent operation of a motor vehicle. The case was heard in Barnstable District Court.

Police and prosecutors said the crash happened around 10:05 p.m. Sunday on West Main Street after a ZZ Top concert at the Cape Cod Melody Tent. They allege a black pickup was traveling at a high rate of speed when it entered a marked crosswalk and hit the officer, who was directing pedestrian traffic.

Prosecutors said the officer was wearing a reflective jacket and holding a flashlight in an illuminated crosswalk with flashing lights. They also alleged that Brando-Hunt’s blood-alcohol level was nearly three times the legal limit; that allegation has not been tested at trial.

The officer was taken first to Cape Cod Hospital and then transferred to a Boston hospital, where he underwent surgery. His condition had not been released. Brando-Hunt’s bail was set at $10,000 cash, and he is due back in court in October.
dek: Prosecutors say a speeding pickup hit a Barnstable officer directing traffic Sunday; the officer underwent surgery and his condition was not released.
headline: Osterville man pleads not guilty after officer struck outside Hyannis concert
